correctness.rationale: An inductive flag-support lemma establishes ten as the least possible induced support and identifies equality with octahedral four-spheres. Every disjoint five-path tuple is enumerated once, giving 912 carriers; all have directly verified zero integer boundary. The acyclic 5,525-pair Morse matching on all 11,067 nonempty faces is independently recomputed, producing ten critical four-cells and six five-cells, with a rank-two primitive integer Morse differential. Its explicit eight-dimensional integral quotient chart sends all 912 cycles to gcd-one vectors. Exhaustive graph automorphism backtracking yields all 96 symmetries, ten orbits, exact ranks and a determinant-one witness in each orbit. The scientific assertions are finite and verified by code included in the same package; this is not an infinite inference from sampling. A separate program recomputes unreduced mod-two boundary ranks (1935 and 1873), checks all 912 cycles individually nonbounding modulo two, and confirms their eight-dimensional overall span; these calculations corroborate but do not substitute for the integral proof.

value.rationale: This is a motivated local-to-global question for the canonical vertex- and edge-transitive cubic Möbius–Kantor graph. The shortest-induced-support threshold, complete 912-carrier census, primitive integral homology images and rank-stratified symmetry orbits measure precise inclusion data invisible to the known ambient wedge decomposition. Four distinct symmetry orbits separately generate the full integral group; other primitive orbit lattices have ranks four or seven. These are structural, non-routine finite results with reusable explicit generators and boundary certificates.
